Exodus

EK-suh-dus — starts like 'exit'; an exodus is everyone exiting together, all at once. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Exodus is a mass departure of a large number of people.

The approaching hurricane triggered a massive exodus of residents from the coastal towns.

Worked Example

A factory that once employed most of a small town suddenly closes its doors for good. Within a year, hundreds of families pack up their belongings and move away, one after another, in search of new jobs elsewhere.

A huge number of people leaving all around the same time, for the same reason, is exactly what an exodus is. Unlike 'trip,' which is usually about one person or a small group, exodus specifically describes a mass departure.

How Exodus Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

departure

departure: the act of leaving a place

migration

migration: movement of a large number of people from one place to another

flight

flight: a hurried escape or departure

Antonyms

arrival

arrival: the act of reaching or coming to a place

influx

influx: a large number of people arriving somewhere

How Strong Is It? — departure → exodus → flight

departure vs. exodus

departure vs. exodus: Departure is a plainer, weaker word than exodus — a departure can describe just one person leaving, while exodus specifically means a huge number of people leaving together.

flight vs. exodus

flight vs. exodus: Flight can feel more urgent than exodus: an exodus can be planned or gradual, but flight suggests a hurried, often desperate escape from danger.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: out (Greek)

Root — od

Root — od: way, road, path (from Greek hodos; its h drops after ex- -- the same root in odometer)

Suffix — -us

Suffix — -us: the Latinized noun ending the word kept when it entered English

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- ('out') + od ('way, road', from Greek hodos) + -us (the Latinized ending) spell exodus: 'the way out.' An exodus is, at its root, a large group finding the road out and leaving together.

Use the root in a new word: odometer

Use the root in a new word: odometer: The odometer showed the car had traveled over one hundred thousand miles on the road.
